name: Foundation for Economic Education

summary.text: The Foundation for Economic Education (FEE) was founded on March 7, 1946 by Leonard E. Read with Henry Hazlitt and others at Irvington, New York. Its founding followed a 1945 capital campaign led by DuPont executive Jasper Crane with Alfred Kohlberg; Harold Luhnow of the William Volker Fund was an early trustee and supporter, and the founding trustees included B.F. Goodrich's David Goodrich and General Motors' Donaldson Brown.

sources.title: The Postwar Renaissance I: Libertarianism (Murray Rothbard)

facts.claim: FEE's own history dates its founding to March 7, 1946 by Leonard E. Read and Henry Hazlitt with associates, in Irvington, New York, where its first headquarters was purchased that year.
facts.quote: Leonard E. Read founded FEE in 1946 as the first "think tank" dedicated to free markets

sources.title: Timeline of the Foundation for Economic Education

facts.claim: A founding officer's recollection published by FEE says Read raised the money and set up the foundation in 1946; the original officers included Goodrich as board chairman, Read as president and Fairchild as secretary, and H. W. Luhnow, president of William Volker & Company, was among the trustees.
facts.quote: H. W. Luhnow, president of William Volker & Company, was among the trustees

facts.claim: Murray Rothbard's account for the Mises Institute says Luhnow (of the Volker Fund) became an active supporter of FEE after the war.
facts.quote: Luhnow became an active supporter of FEE after the war

sources.title: The Postwar Renaissance I: Libertarianism (Murray Rothbard)

facts.claim: FEE's founding followed a 1945 capital campaign started by DuPont executive Jasper Crane with Alfred Kohlberg; founding trustees included Dave Goodrich of B.F. Goodrich, Donaldson Brown of General Motors, Henry Hazlitt, Fred Fairchild, Leo Wolman and Claude Robinson.
facts.quote: Jasper Crane, a DuPont executive, started a capital campaign in 1945 with Alfred Kohlberg

connections.claim: Leonard Read founded FEE in 1946 and was its first president.
connections.quote: Leonard E. Read founded FEE in 1946

Howard Pew, Inland Steel, Quaker Oats and Sears are named as early contributors only in a tertiary summary; FEE's own pages opened do not name them, so this needs a primary source before being recorded.
